sentences: Optimistically universal online learning asks for one rule that succeeds on every input process for which universal learning is possible.
For bounded losses, the source also proposes characterizing those processes by how slowly they visit new cells of every countable measurable partition.
The required number of visited cells grows sublinearly with time.
The passage frames both the algorithm and characterization as questions in its historical setting.

Later work cited elsewhere in the collection reports progress on the algorithmic question, so developing this record further requires separating that history from the exact remaining process-characterization task.
working_summary.note: Historical optimistically universal learning question; the later paper stored with TCS-2654 reports a positive deterministic-target result, so algorithmic and process-characterization variants require separate review.
